newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Surging Australian dlr finds a willing buyer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Surging Australian dlr finds a willing buyer.

text.p: The Australian dollar traded above US$0.8000 for the first time in three months and strode to fresh four year highs against the yen as one European buyer bought the currency in volume on Friday.
Traders put the size of the buying at at least A$500 million on the day, and said it may be the same buyer who had purchased a similar amount of Aussie earlier this week.
"A lot of demand this afternoon," one bank trader said. "There just seems to have been one German gentleman buying it most of the day, and it's just quite awesome really."

By 4.45 p.m. (0545 GMT) the dollar was at US$0.7988/93, having surged on a break of resistance at US$0.7960 to trade to a high of US$0.8005/10, and ending well up on an opening US$0.7930/35 and Thursday's local close of US$0.7911/16. It was the dollar's first foray above US$0.8000 since December.
"One guy out there is just buying, buying, buying, at the moment," a U.S. bank trader said.

"Every time it dips down they put out another round of calls and up she goes again. It's been relentless," he said, adding that it appeared to be the same buyer who had bought around A$700 million earlier this week.
The break above US$0.7960 was important as it represented the 61.8 Fibonacci retracement level of the dollar's fall from a six year high of US$0.8212 in December to February's low of US$0.7550.

While the dollar had breached US$0.8000, sell orders had forced it back slightly. However, traders said the dollar was looking well positioned for further gains, especially given the volume of the buy order.
"I think the guy has probably bought anything from A$500 million to three quarters (of a billion dollars), somewhere in that region," the local bank dealer said.
"It's looking very strong...the demand is still out there no question about that," he said of the dollar.
The size of the initial buying had led to shortcovering and triggered some computer model related buying, traders said.
If the dollar cleared the US$0.8000 level, resistance would be expected around US$0.8020/30, while US$0.7960 was expected to provide support.
Traders said while the yen cross had risen strongly to its highest levels since May 1992, the afternoon buying had been dominated by straight Australian dollar buying.
"Particularly this morning there was certainly some Aussie/yen volume going through, but I think a lot of this stuff this afternoon is just Aussie," the local bank dealer said.

The Aussie/yen was at 98.74/84 in late trade, having made large gains from an early 97.86/96 and a local close on Thursday of 96.66/76. Strength in the U.S. dollar had benefitted the cross rate, traders said.
In trade weighted terms, the afternoon strength saw the dollar rise to 61.5, its highest level since October 1990, up on an opening 61.1 and a close of 60.8.

While the market was seeing the volume, traders were unsure of the purpose of the buying spree this week. If the lead buyer was the same player who had bought around A$700 million earlier this week, it meant that well over A$1 billion had been bought, they said.

"I'd love to know what they're up to," the U.S. bank trader said. "I'd love to know what all this Aussie's been bought for...I don't know whether it's an acquisition or something like that, but it certainly is a truckload of money."
